items.title: What One Bad Night Of Sleep Did To My Blood Sugar
items.summary: Sleep and metabolic health are more connected than most people realize, and this was a chance to see it play out in real data while traveling. After a night with only 6 hours and 24 minutes of sleep, average glucose rose 10 points and waking glucose increased 3 points compared to a night with over 8 hours. Just one night of poor sleep can raise hunger hormones like ghrelin and elevate blood sugar, which is why consistent, high-quality sleep is one of the more overlooked levers for metabolic health, especially for women. #GlucoseMonitoring #SleepHealth #MetabolicHealth #FemaleLongevity #ContinuousGlucoseMonitor #WomensHealth #SleepScience

We are building a vertically integrated pharmaceutical company with software for prescribing, telehealth, compounding, manufacturing, and delivery. We are starting with GLP-1s and peptides. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. items.title: Your Indoor Air May Be Working Against Your Health
items.summary: Air is one of our largest daily exposures and one of the easiest to ignore because you cannot see most pollutants. I do not think home optimization should begin with buying every gadget. It should begin with measurement. PM2.5, VOCs, humidity, and CO2 can reveal whether cooking, cleaning products, poor ventilation, smoke, or an overcrowded room are changing the air you breathe. Once you know the problem, interventions become more rational: ventilation when outdoor air is clean, source control, appropriate filtration, and regular maintenance. A plant may improve the feel of a room, but it should not replace filtration or ventilation. My approach is to make the environments where I spend the most time as supportive as realistically possible, rather than trying to control every exposure in the world. #IndoorAirQuality #HealthyHome #AirPollution #EnvironmentalHealth #Longevity

items.title: Starting Exercise During Pregnancy Is Not Too Late
items.summary: This myth needed to be retired a long time ago. Dr. Margie Davenport explains that women who were inactive before pregnancy and started moving during it saw a 40 percent reduction in pregnancy complications like gestational diabetes, preeclampsia, and gestational hypertension, a 67 percent reduction in depression risk, and no increase in miscarriage, small baby, or early baby risk. The old idea that you shouldn't start something new once you're pregnant just isn't supported by the data. #pregnancyexercise #womenshealth #longevity #prenatalfitness #exerciseinpregnancy

items.title: 3 Longevity Drugs I QUIT (And the 4 I Take Instead)
items.summary: The 3 "Longevity Drugs" That Fail the Data, and 4 Repurposed Ones Worth Considering Back with another solo episode, this one on Big Pharma! Metformin, rapamycin, and statins are three of the most trusted names in longevity, and none of them hold up the way you've been told. This episode breaks down the human data behind the drugs everyone assumes are safe, and reveals four lesser-known repurposed pharmaceuticals that might do more for your metabolism, mitochondria, and lifespan. Dave walks through why metformin blunts the muscle-building signal your body needs from exercise, why rapamycin's stunning mouse studies fell apart in the 2025 PEARL trial, and why statins help one person in a hundred while draining the CoQ10 your mitochondria depend on. Then he lays out the yes list: tadalafil for vascular and brain health, SGLT2 inhibitors for metabolic and kidney protection, acarbose for gut and longevity markers, and low dose naltrexone for calming an overactive immune system. Host Dave Asprey is the father of biohacking, founder of Danger Coffee and Smarter Not Harder, and a New York Times bestselling author who has spent decades studying human performance, functional medicine, and the science of not aging. As co-founder of Unlimited.Life, a concierge longevity practice that runs over $50,000 in lab work per client, he pulls back the curtain on what the data actually shows once you strip away the marketing. This is essential listening for anyone serious about biohacking…
